quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How should drivers use a shared center lane on a road with traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: To slow down or stop before turning left
As an extra travel lane when traffic is slow

questions.correctAnswerText: To slow down or stop before turning left
questions.explanation: A shared center lane is only for slowing down or stopping to make a safe left turn. It is not a travel lane and cannot be used for passing.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow on a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and expect oncoming traffic to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes dangerous fumes from your vehicle. If it leaks, harmful carbon monoxide can enter the passenger area. Fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp right turn in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp right turn in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a sharp right turn is coming.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line when:

options.text: Doing so would interfere with traffic.
The car in front of you is disabled.
Passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stay farther behind other vehicles. Your car may need more time to stop than on dry roads.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time:

options.text: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. You can then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection is ahead with a road joining from the right.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Does not change blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee cannot lower your blood alcohol level. While it may help you stay awake, it does not change your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
The suggested speed to drive on a road when conditions are ideal.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. Slow down in school zones, work zones, or when bad weather or road construction make the speed unsafe.

questions.question: When you see an accident, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived yet.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Focus on your driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Never drive to an accident, fire, or disaster just to look.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is safe and reasonable.
A speed that is safe for the current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not drive faster than what is safe and reasonable. Drive at a speed that matches the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and light. Always follow the legal speed limit.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are pointing downward. This signal means the driver plans to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles toward the left. This means:
questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road marks its edge. When the edge line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign alerts you that bicycles may cross the road.

questions.question: A sign with a red circle and a slash through it means:

options.text: Some drivers must yield to others.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are rectangular with white, red, and black markings. A red circle with a slash means the action shown is forbidden.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign:

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Curve and turn signs often show a recommended speed for those areas. You may feel comfortable driving faster in good weather, but never do so in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: Your vehicle is moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing bicycles because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road. Always be extra careful around bicyclists.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal after you start moving into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before turning in a residential area. On a freeway, signal at least 5 seconds before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with slow, steady pressure.

questions.question: Your body gets rid of about how many alcoholic drinks per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One drink an hour.
questions.explanation: The average person processes about one drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on many factors: how much you drink, how fast you drink, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When can you use a shared center turn lane?

options.text: To make a left turn onto another street, road, or driveway.
To make a right turn onto another street, road, or highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: To make a left turn onto another street, road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: You can only use a shared center turn lane to make a left turn. It is not a travel lane and you cannot use it to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the least traffic.
On the same side as traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the most traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road that faces the traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you approach it. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must always let them pass first.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
You should slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can clearly see oncoming traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see oncoming traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting road where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Tell someone "No thanks, I'm driving" if they offer you a drink.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: To avoid drinking and driving, decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices once you have started drinking.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand upward, they are signaling they will turn right. Watch for this signal and adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped ahead with its lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it space. If changing lanes is not safe or there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop at an emergency scene.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is coming toward you with its lights or sirens on. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly while staying to the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: On any road, you must yield to an emergency vehicle using its lights or siren. Move as far right as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by what color lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When should you use your parking brake?

options.text: Only when parking on a hill
Only when parked in a driveway

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake when you park. Turn off the engine, set the parking brake, and take your keys. Do not rely on the transmission alone to hold your vehicle.

questions.question: You have a green light and want to turn left, but traffic coming toward you is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: If traffic is coming toward you, wait for it to pass before turning left. You may enter the intersection to prepare for your left turn when the light is green and no car ahead is turning left.

questions.question: You are on a highway with two solid yellow lines. When may you cross them?

options.text: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
To pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without using emergency signals. What should you do?

options.text: Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you without its siren or flashing lights on, you do not need to pull over. Just drive normally.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator is stuck open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, the car will keep going even with your foot off the pedal. Turn off the ignition using care to avoid locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in a car's blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is or how fast it is going. Always watch carefully for motorcycles.

questions.question: Which does NOT affect how far a vehicle takes to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, how much your vehicle weighs, your brakes, your tires, the road surface, and your speed. The time of day does not matter.

questions.question: What sign is this?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: This is a triangle-shaped Yield sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other vehicles go first. Stop only if you need to.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the car to go.
Opposite to the direction of the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the car to go. Once the car starts to straighten, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: You see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line. The broken line is on your side. Can you pass?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass. Cross the lines only if no cars are coming from the other direction.

questions.question: What color curb means you can only park for a short time?
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: A white curb means short stops only.

questions.question: You turn onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction. Which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to where you came from.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to the lane you were in before. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Get ready to stop because the light will turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and be careful. Look both ways before crossing.

questions.question: How should you look ahead to prepare for hazards?

options.text: Scan the entire road and both sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the entire road and both sides.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to spot problems early. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Scan the whole road, including both sides, to see hazards before they happen.
